title: Pointwise finite-flat groupoid chart with one identified stabilizer
statement: Work over a field $k$ [def-weil-field], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space], and stacks, representability and 2-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Representable morphism properties are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Flatness, local finite presentation, etaleness and properness use [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. A stack morphism is separated if its relative diagonal is proper. The inertia stack $I_{\mathcal A}$ has objects $(a,\alpha)$ with $a\in\mathcal A(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$, and arrows given by conjugating isomorphisms. Its projection forgets $\alpha$. Finite inertia means that every scheme base change of this projection is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The set $|\mathcal A|$ consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism after common field extension, with the atlas topology [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. A scheme groupoid $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ has the laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Its quotient $[U/R]$ is the fppf stackification of the groupoid of $T$-points, using [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Finite locally free means finite, flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $\mathcal X/k$ have finite inertia, and let $x\in|\mathcal X|$. There exist affine $k$-schemes $U,R$, a scheme groupoid $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ with $s,t$ finite locally free, a morphism $h:\mathcal V=[U/R]\to\mathcal X$ representable by algebraic spaces and etale, and $v\in|\mathcal V|$ mapping to $x$, such that $h$ identifies the stabilizer group schemes at $v$ and $x$. This identification is understood after choosing a common field over which the two points and their comparison isomorphism are represented; it is an isomorphism of group schemes, not just of their rational points.

source.place: Tag 0DU4 (lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM-at-x), specialized to finite inertia; its hypotheses follow from Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), parts (1),(5), and finite morphisms being separated and locally quasi-finite (morphisms.tex Tags 01WN, 02NU).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-inertia-flat-quasifinite-presentation] to obtain $p:U\to\mathcal X$, $u\in U$ over $x$, and the scheme self-relation $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ with separated, flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite projections. The stabilizer fibre $G_u$ is the scheme base change of $I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$ along the object $p(u):\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to\mathcal X$: on every test scheme over this field, both descriptions are the automorphisms of that object. Thus $G_u$ is finite by the finite-inertia hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0DU4 (lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM-at-x), first paragraph: scheme presentation and finiteness of G_u

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-etale-groupoid-affine-stabilizer-splitting] to $(U,R)$ and $u$. Its separatedness, flatness, local finite presentation and local quasi-finiteness hypotheses are provided by step 1, and $G_u$ is finite. Obtain affine $U'$, an etale $q:U'\to U$, a point $u'$ with the same residue field, and an open subgroupoid $P\subset R'=U'\times_U R\times_U U'$ finite, flat and locally finitely presented over $U'$ in both projections, containing the entire stabilizer fibre over $u'$. The canonical identification $R'\simeq U'\times_{\mathcal X}U'$ sends a triple $(a,r,b)$ to the objects $a,b$ and the isomorphism between $p(q(a))$ and $p(q(b))$ specified by $r$; the inverse reads off those same three entries. It respects identity, inverse and composition. This supplies the fibre-product detail omitted in the source.

source.place: Tag 0DU4, second paragraph, using spaces-more-groupoids.tex Tag 0DTE (lemma-splitting-affine-scheme)

proof.text: Put $p'=pq:U'\to\mathcal X$. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $p'$ is representable, flat and locally of finite presentation. Its image $D\subseteq|\mathcal X|$ is open by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. Choose a smooth surjective atlas $A\to\mathcal X$. The open subset $D_A\subseteq A$ lying above $D$ is invariant under $A\times_{\mathcal X}A$, since the two projections of a field-valued arrow represent the same point of $\mathcal X$. By [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] it defines an open algebraic substack $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal X$. That lemma's factorization criterion makes $p'$ factor through $\mathcal W$, and $U'\to\mathcal W$ is surjective: each field-valued object of $\mathcal W$ has its point in the image of $U'$, so lifts after a common field extension. Flatness and local finite presentation follow by base change to $\mathcal W$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations] to get $[U'/R']\simeq\mathcal W$, compatibly with $p'$.

source.place: Tag 0DU4, replacement by the open image; algebraic.tex Tag 04WY (remark-flat-fp-presentation); stacks-properties.tex Tags 04XL (lemma-topology-points), 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks), and 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation)

proof.text: The projections of $R'$ are flat and locally of finite presentation: they are the base changes of $p'$. Apply [lem-sfb-open-subgroupoid-etale-quotient] to the open subgroupoid $P\subset R'$ to obtain an algebraic stack $\mathcal V=[U'/P]$ and a representable etale map $\mathcal V\to[U'/R']\simeq\mathcal W$. The open immersion $\mathcal W\to\mathcal X$ is representable etale: its scheme base changes are open immersions, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Composition is representable etale by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], giving $h:\mathcal V\to\mathcal X$. Since $U'$ is affine and $P\to U'$ is finite, $P$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](b). Both projections of $P$ are finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Thus $(U',P)$ supplies the required affine groupoid.

source.place: Tag 0DU4, final paragraph: Tag 0DU2 (lemma-quasi-splitting-etale), affineness and finite-flat projections

proof.text: Let $v$ be the image of $u'$ in $\mathcal V$. Then $h(v)=x$, represented over $\kappa(u')=\kappa(u)$ by $p(q(u'))$. Clause (1) of [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations] identifies the self-relation of $U'\to[U'/P]$ with $P$ and that of $U'\to[U'/R']$ with $R'$. Pulling these identifications back along the pair $(u',u')$ identifies the stabilizer map with $P_{(u',u')}\to R'_{(u',u')}=G_{u'}$. This is an open subscheme inclusion whose underlying image is all of $G_{u'}$ by the splitting property of step 2. An open subscheme with the entire underlying space has the same restricted structure sheaf, so this inclusion is an isomorphism of schemes, including all nilpotents. Composition of arrows restricts from $R'$ to $P$, so the isomorphism respects multiplication, identity and inverse. The equivalence with the full open substack $\mathcal W\subset\mathcal X$ preserves these automorphism groups. This proves the required isomorphism of stabilizer group schemes over the common representing field.

source.place: Tag 0DU4, last sentence: containment of the whole stabilizer, not only its rational points
